_note: Mana: the definition from Lehmann (CW8 ¶128) and the primitive energetics around it (¶130, ¶127, ¶129), its presence in Jung's own field observations (CW10 ¶128, CW16 ¶4), the mana-personality (CW7 ¶388), and its late appearances as conscience and as the effect of depth (CW10 ¶845, ¶583). Quotations are placed by the corpus; nothing is typed.
line: The sensed dynamism older than any theory of it: an extraordinary effectiveness that can attach to persons and things — Jung's bridge from primitive energetics to psychic energy.

sections.title: The definition
sections.line: The word arrives from ethnology with a deliberately vague sense — 'extraordinarily effective' — and Jung keeps the vagueness.

quotes.quote: In his classic study of mana Lehmann defines it as something "extraordinarily effective."
We cannot escape the impression that the primitive view of mana is a forerunner of our concept of psychic energy and, most probably, of energy in general.

sections.title: An experience, not a concept
sections.line: Mana is not a primitive theory of energy but the perception of a relation — it is present in the moment something shows itself as more than itself.

quotes.quote: In the face of something extraordinary it is not he who is astonished, but rather the thing which is astonishing.
Mana is a universal medicinal or healing power which renders men, animals, and plants fruitful and endows chieftain and medicine-man with magical strength.
even at early levels of human consciousness man felt the need to represent the sensed dynamism of psychic events in a concrete way

sections.title: The reservations
sections.line: Jung keeps the term honest: it is a representation, not a concept, and nothing divine attaches to it.

quotes.quote: Thus mana is not a concept but a representation based on the perception of a "phenomenal" relationship.
nothing "divine" attaches to mana, so that one cannot see in mana the original form of an idea of God.

sections.title: The mana-personality
sections.line: When the ego takes the charge for itself, the archetype is worn as a person: the magician, the great man, the woman who knows.

quotes.quote: It corresponds to a dominant of the collective unconscious, to an archetype which has taken shape in the human psyche through untold ages of just that kind of experience.

sections.title: Mana now
sections.line: The word never leaves Jung's late vocabulary: conscience itself is a manifestation of it.

quotes.quote: Conscience is a manifestation of mana, of the “extraordinarily powerful,” a quality which is the especial peculiarity of archetypal ideas.
The deepening and broadening of his consciousness produce the kind of effect which the primitives call “mana.”
